Zhang Shi, as the grandmother, certainly wouldn’t bother with such details. Lord Bo might have the intention, but as a man, he wouldn’t have the ability to spot the discrepancies.

And Liu Shi, a woman well-versed in the ways of the inner quarters, didn’t need to see it with her own eyes to know the tricks being played. On the surface, the dowry had sixty-eight large chests, but apart from the first few, which were decent, the rest were increasingly lacking. Many of the chests weren’t even filled, and the valuable ornaments, jade and porcelain pieces, and even the expensive fabrics and silks that had been prepared were likely replaced with imitations, worth very little.

Even more outrageous were the estate and the shops. She had paid special attention to these. The estate to be given as part of the dowry was at least seven or eight days’ journey from the capital. It was the smallest and most remote estate in the Bo family’s properties, with only a few dozen acres of inferior land. The annual harvest was barely enough to sustain the people living there. It had been kept only as a property for an unfavored concubine’s son in case the family was divided in the future.

As for the two shops, although they were in the capital, they were located in remote and poor areas of the marketplace. They were two insignificant sundry shops. Compared to the Bo family’s other properties, which could earn thousands or even tens of thousands of taels a year, these two shops were lucky not to be losing money—there was no hope of them making a profit.

In high-ranking families, the mistress of the household could make life difficult for an unfavored daughter simply through the dowry, leaving her with no way to defend herself.

Yu Qingci was the daughter of that wretched woman, Su Chengniang, who was Lord Bo’s original wife. If it weren’t for the Old Madam’s opportunistic decision to demote her to a concubine, Qiao Shi wouldn’t have her current position. As the mistress of the household, how could Qiao Shi wholeheartedly provide a generous dowry for Su Chengniang’s daughter? Naturally, she would take this opportunity to cut corners with the dowry.

So, on the surface, the ten-li red dowry was just a hollow show to deceive outsiders.

---

chapters.title: Restoring Reputation
chapters.content:
No one had expected Lord Bo to suddenly bring up the matter of displaying the dowry, catching Qiao Shi completely off guard. Liu Shi found this amusing and was eager to see how Qiao Shi would handle the situation.

After leaving the Shouyin Hall, Qiao Shi didn’t stop until she reached a secluded spot, where she finally let out a long breath. She angrily shook off Wu Mom’s supporting hand and gritted her teeth. "It must be that wretched woman’s idea! Otherwise, how would Lord Bo suddenly think of displaying the dowry? She’s everywhere, truly like a lingering ghost!"

Wu Mom cautiously looked around before lowering her voice. "Madam, please calm down. Who would have thought that wretched woman would be so troublesome and always one step ahead of us? But since Lord Bo has given the order, this matter must proceed. It seems we can’t avoid tomorrow’s display."

"If we really put out the dowry we’ve prepared, and if someone with a keen eye notices, it won’t end well."

Qiao Shi snapped, "It’s not ‘if’—it’s certain they’ll notice! Do you take everyone for fools?"

Wu Mom knew the situation was difficult, so she reminded her, "Madam, time is tight. What should we do now?"

Qiao Shi gritted her teeth in frustration. "If Lord Bo had mentioned this earlier, we could have found a way to handle it. But he had to bring it up now, with the display tomorrow and the boxes to be sealed and taken away immediately after. How can we make any changes? This is infuriating!"

During the wedding, all the dowry items were placed in large red sandalwood chests. Outsiders could only see the top layer in each chest. As for what was at the bottom, they could only rely on the master of ceremonies reading from the dowry list.

As for the estate and shops, only the property deeds were displayed, usually placed on a layer of bright red silk. But those were just a few thin sheets of paper. Unless someone was rude enough to pick them up and examine them closely, who would know the size or location of the estate or shops?

By the time all the rituals were completed, even if the bride later discovered discrepancies with the dowry list, the marriage would already be finalized, and there would be nothing she could do about it.

Of course, such mismatches between the actual items and the dowry list were rare. Either the natal family was trying to save face by passing off inferior goods as superior, or the bride was an unfavored concubine’s daughter.

But Yu Qingci was the daughter of that wretched woman. Why should she have a ten-li red dowry?

These days, Qiao Shi had personally overseen every detail of the wedding preparations, precisely to prevent that mother and daughter from gaining even the slightest advantage from the Bo family. She had swapped out anything in the dowry where she could cut corners—jewelry, antiques, jade, paintings, and even expensive Shu brocade and Yun Duan silk had all been replaced with cheap imitations that looked good on the surface.

But if those items were displayed in broad daylight, anyone with a discerning eye would see the truth immediately. The Bo family’s reputation would be ruined.

Thinking of this, Qiao Shi let out a long, stifled breath and squeezed out through gritted teeth, "Let’s go back and discuss this."

Wu Mom said nothing, simply supporting Qiao Shi as they walked back.

Once they returned to the Haitang Courtyard, Qiao Shi collapsed onto the noble consort’s couch, her legs weak and her body devoid of strength. She knew this was from anger.

Wu Mom gently advised, "Madam, things have come to this. You should let it go. They’re just external possessions. In exchange, we secure Second Young Miss’s future. There will be plenty of opportunities to deal with them later."

Qiao Shi understood this logic all too well, but time was pressing, and she had no choice. She ordered Wu Mom, "You personally oversee this. Replace all those items with the originals. Don’t let anyone notice."

"Yes, this old servant will arrange it immediately."

Wu Mom sighed and turned to leave. The thought of giving that girl a large sum of genuine, high-quality items made both mistress and servant feel as if they were on the verge of death.

But they both knew that, for now, they had to endure this. Otherwise, when the chests were opened tomorrow in front of everyone, there would be no way to cover it up.

The next morning, the entrance of the Bo family was already decorated with lanterns and banners to welcome the guests.

Although the actual wedding was the next day, the Bo family had deliberately spread the word about the dowry display to attract more relatives and friends.

The more people, the livelier and more joyous the occasion.

So, apart from the General’s mansion, which had already arranged for a procession to deliver the dowry, many relatives and friends who had heard the news also came to join in the festivities.

In recent days, some news had already spread. It was said that the South Ping Bo family’s marriage alliance with the Ningyuan General’s mansion had switched from the eldest daughter to the daughter of a concubine who had returned home unexpectedly. Many were curious. Unfortunately, the Bo family had kept that concubine’s daughter well hidden, so no one had actually seen her.

Although she likely wouldn’t appear at today’s dowry display, coming to join the excitement and gather some information was still an interesting prospect.

Thus, the number of guests today was exceptionally high.

Under everyone’s gaze, South Ping Bo Yu Jingcheng personally brought Yu Qingci and her younger brother, Yu Qingbai, before the crowd. He solemnly introduced them to the guests, declaring that the siblings were born of his original wife, and that their mother, Su, was currently living outside the family due to mourning customs and thus unable to appear.

The guests were immediately stunned. Wasn’t she supposed to be the daughter of a concubine? How could she be the legitimate daughter of the original wife? Were the rumors circulating in the capital false?

Upon closer inspection, the siblings were both strikingly handsome, with appearances and demeanor that were in no way inferior to the children of the capital’s noble families, who had been carefully raised with great care. Those who knew the Bo family’s past immediately accepted the explanation.

Moreover, the head of the family, South Ping Bo, had even presented the family genealogy. This matter was undoubtedly settled.

So that was how it was. It turned out that to protect the eldest legitimate daughter from marrying into the Shouwang Gate as a widow, the Bo family had secretly brought back the concubine’s daughter who had been raised outside to take her place. But in reality, it was the true legitimate daughter replacing the half-legitimate one. The Bo family’s actions were admirable.

So the so-called Madam of the Bo family was just a secondary wife. Then, in the eyes of the world, the Bo family’s eldest daughter, Yu Qingyan, was actually the daughter of a secondary wife?

The guests immediately began whispering among themselves, and some even praised Yu Jingcheng on the spot.

Qiao Shi was already furious about the dowry display, but she never expected Lord Bo to suddenly announce the siblings’ identities in front of everyone. This was undoubtedly a move to restore their reputation, and it nearly made her faint from anger.

Yu Qingyan and her sister, Yu Qingying, were no better off. They had been entertaining a few close friends who had come to join the festivities when their father suddenly announced Yu Qingci and Yu Qingbai’s legitimate status in front of all the guests. The sisters were immediately humiliated. Yu Qingying burst into tears and ran back to her own courtyard.

Yu Qingyan, to avoid public criticism, had to grit her teeth and maintain her composure in front of others, which only made her close friends feel more sympathy for her.

Yu Qingyan allowed herself to show a hint of grievance, but in her heart, she vowed: I will remember today’s humiliation, Yu Qingci. In the future, I will repay you tenfold, a hundredfold!

chapters.title: A Rich Dowry
chapters.content:
The people of the Marquis's mansion carried out the sixty-eight palanquins of the bride's dowry one by one and displayed them in front of everyone. The onlookers, curious, couldn’t help but comment on each item.

It had to be said, the Marquis’s mansion had prepared a very substantial dowry for this daughter. It was in no way inferior to that of other noble families' legitimate daughters. It seemed the rumors outside were true—the Marquis of Nanping truly doted on this daughter who had returned to the family late in life. Otherwise, he wouldn’t have provided such a rich dowry for her.

As the saying goes, "When the person leaves, the tea cools." The Ningyuan General’s mansion was now a mere empty shell, a far cry from its former glory. The bride was to enter the family tomorrow holding a spirit tablet, doomed to a life of loneliness and hardship. Without a rich dowry to support her, how could she endure such a life?

From this perspective, the Marquis of Nanping’s mansion had won another wave of public favor with this move.

Watching the scene before them, the crowd felt a mix of emotions toward the third legitimate daughter who was about to marry into a household of widowhood—some curiosity, some admiration, but mostly sighs of pity.

Meanwhile, Madame Qiao’s resentment had reached its peak.

Ever since she learned that the Marquis was going to display the dowry, she had been unable to remain calm. Last night, she had ordered Mama Wu to replace all the items on the list with the finest alternatives. So now, everything displayed before the crowd was of the highest quality, yet all of it was to be given to that low-born daughter. From yesterday until now, she had endured and endured, barely suppressing the rage in her heart.

Su-shi, just you wait!

A commotion arose in the front courtyard. The sharp, high-pitched voice of a eunuch announced the arrival of an imperial decree. Madame Qiao, flustered, had no time to speak before hastily sending someone to notify the Old Madame and the Marquis.

It turned out that the palace had sent an envoy. The Emperor, moved by the Marquis of Nanping’s loyalty in honoring his promise and showing compassion for the soon-to-be bride, had bestowed upon her a gift of jewelry, fine silks, and auspicious ornaments—enough to fill six large boxes.

Madame Qiao knelt on the ground, listening to the decree, her throat burning with a metallic taste. She swayed, nearly collapsing.

Yü Jingcheng and the others, however, were overjoyed. After rising, they warmly received the eunuch who had delivered the decree.

With the Emperor setting an example, many families who were close to the Marquis’s mansion soon followed suit, sending additional dowry gifts. Yü Jingcheng personally expressed his gratitude and then had these gifts added to the dowry procession.

After this episode, the grandeur and prestige of the Marquis’s mansion that day were witnessed by all present. It would undoubtedly be the talk of the town for a long time to come—but that is a story for another time.

Amid the crowd’s complicated gazes, all the dowry was soon sealed and carried out of the Marquis’s mansion one by one. This time, leading the procession were the six large boxes wrapped in red silk, bestowed by the palace. The three-foot-tall red coral tree and the jade ruyi from the Empress were prominently displayed before the crowd.

As the procession passed through a street not far from Liuli Alley, another group arrived with drums and gongs, bringing additional dowry gifts. This time, the number of gifts even surpassed the palace’s bestowal—twenty-four palanquins in total.

At the front was a middle-aged steward, who loudly announced that these were additional dowry gifts specially prepared by the Marquis of Nanping’s official wife for her daughter, along with four rooms of servants to accompany her.

Su Chengniang had originally prepared far more than twenty-four palanquins of dowry for her daughter. Upon learning of her daughter’s impending marriage, she had begun gathering all the treasures she had saved over the years, packing them into boxes. It was only after much persuasion from Yü Qingci that she had restrained herself and reduced the number of boxes.

Moreover, she had sent people to inquire about the General’s mansion in detail. Rumor had it that the inner quarters were far from peaceful. As the saying goes, "A jade stone invites theft." Since her daughter would be marrying as a widow with no husband to rely on, an overly rich dowry might instead attract unwanted attention. If her daughter, weak and alone, were to suffer losses, it wouldn’t be worth it.

After much deliberation, she had settled on these twenty-four palanquins. But secretly, she had given her daughter a total of one hundred thousand taels in silver notes as a hidden dowry. This sum was not recorded on the dowry list—only she and her daughter knew of it. This way, it wouldn’t attract the attention of irrelevant people and would serve as an extra layer of security for her daughter.

It had to be said that Su Chengniang had truly gone to great lengths for her daughter. Over the years, while managing the household, she had also learned to do business. Though she couldn’t claim to be wildly successful, after more than a decade, she had accumulated a considerable fortune. Sending her daughter off with a grand dowry was an easy task for her—she didn’t need to rely on anyone’s favor.

By the time the dowry procession arrived at the General’s mansion, Yü Qingci’s dowry had grown to one hundred and six palanquins—far more than originally prepared. Not only the Marquis’s mansion but almost everyone at the General’s mansion was stunned.

These dowry items, along with some of the accompanying servants from the Marquis’s mansion, were directly moved into the prepared courtyard in the General’s mansion. They would be properly arranged once the bride arrived.

The next day was the wedding. That night, Ziteng Courtyard was quiet. Yü Qingci had only Tong’er and Mama Pei, whom Su Chengniang had sent, by her side.

Mama Pei was an elderly servant who had been with Su Chengniang for over a decade. Initially, Su Chengniang had wanted to give her daughter Mama Liu, but her daughter had refused. So this time, Su Chengniang had sent Mama Pei, along with her contract of servitude, to be by her daughter’s side. She wanted another trusted elder to look after her.

With an experienced elder like Mama Pei by her side, Su Chengniang could rest a little easier.

This time, Yü Qingci did not refuse and kept Mama Pei.

Of course, Madame Qiao had also prepared two rooms of servants and two maids to accompany her, one of whom was Siqin, who had attended to her for a period of time. These people had already followed the dowry procession to the General’s mansion earlier that day. At this moment, they were probably guarding her courtyard and the dowry in the General’s mansion.

After the wedding tomorrow, she would take full control of everything.

Mama Pei was new, but she had years of experience managing the inner quarters by her mistress’s side, so she quickly adapted to handling the trivial matters around Yü Qingci. Moreover, she treated Yü Qingci with great respect, which pleased Yü Qingci. She was indeed a trusted servant who had been with her mother for many years.

At this moment, Mama Pei kept glancing toward the courtyard gate. Was she waiting for someone?

After Mama Pei looked outside for the Nth time, Yü Qingci couldn’t help but ask, "Mama Pei, are you waiting for someone?"

Mama Pei, staring outside with a displeased expression, said, "Miss, you’re getting married tomorrow. How can the Marquis’s mansion not even send someone to check on you? It’s already this late. Normally, elders should come to see the bride, fulfilling their duties properly. At the very least, they should send other young ladies from the mansion to keep you company. This doesn’t look like the night before a wedding at all. I must say, the Marquis’s mansion’s customs are lacking."

Yü Qingci smiled indifferently. "This is fine. It’s peaceful and free from trouble. Having you and Tong’er by my side is enough. Besides, with a marriage like mine, there’s no need for the elders to come specially to give advice."

Mama Pei saw how calm she was and couldn’t help but feel a pang of heartache. What a good young lady—just like her mother, she had been a beauty since childhood. Now, she had grown into a delicate, flower-like young woman, yet she was being sent off by this accursed Marquis’s mansion to a life of widowhood. Her entire life was ruined.

---

chapters.title: The Wedding
chapters.content:
The young lady might not feel it now, but in a few years, a decade, or even the decades to come, how would she endure it? Damn that Marquis!

Mama Pei cursed silently in her heart, but she didn’t dare show the slightest bit of it on her face, fearing that the young lady would see and feel distressed as well.

In most families, at a time like this, elders would come to give the bride those somewhat embarrassing gifts and educate her about the wedding night, serving as a kind of preemptive lesson so that she wouldn’t make a fool of herself when the time came.

Though the young lady might not have any use for such knowledge, the customs still required the elders to come and remind her.

But clearly, the Marquis’s mansion was not an ordinary family.

Mama Pei didn’t know that the mistress of the household, Madame Qiao, had been so infuriated by the day’s stimulating events that she had nearly vomited blood on the spot. At this moment, she was clutching her chest, lying in her own courtyard, unable to get up—how could she think of visiting Yü Qingci, the daughter about to leave the family?

Not only did she not come, but she had also instructed her daughters early that morning not to go to Ziteng Courtyard again. The matter of the substitute marriage was now set in stone, leaving no room for regret.

But at this moment, Yü Qingci didn’t care whether anyone accompanied her or not. Having Mama Pei and Tong’er by her side was enough. Moreover, tomorrow she would be entering the General’s mansion holding a spirit tablet—there would be no wedding night, so what did it matter whether she had that kind of knowledge beforehand?

Tong’er entered from outside and said, "Mama Pei, Mama Wu just came by to inform us that the makeup artist, Madame Quanfu, will only arrive at the si hour tomorrow. Does that mean we can wake up at our usual time tomorrow?"

Mama Pei was alarmed. "What? Si hour? Did you hear correctly? Which family’s bride doesn’t get up before the fifth watch to start dressing and applying makeup? The customs here in the capital are different from other places!"

Yü Qingci raised an eyebrow, understanding the situation. She calmly reassured Mama Pei, "Actually, arriving at si hour is fine. It means we can sleep a little longer. We’re not in a hurry to get into the bridal sedan."

Tong’er didn’t quite understand, but Mama Pei and Yü Qingci knew full well that normally, a bride would be woken up before the fifth watch to bathe, change clothes, and apply makeup. All the while, the female elders of the family would chatter on with various instructions, afraid that time would run out.

But Mama Wu had come to deliver this message on Madame Qiao’s orders. Madame Qiao had used the display of the dowry to force their hand, making it so they couldn’t tamper with the dowry. This had backfired on her, costing her a great deal, so naturally, she was displeased and sought to vent her frustration elsewhere.

What Madame Qiao didn’t know was that Yü Qingci was not a young girl marrying for the first time. She no longer cared about these pre-wedding customs and etiquette.

After soothing Mama Pei, Yü Qingci slept soundly and lazily, only rising from bed at dawn to bathe and change clothes at a leisurely pace. By the time Madame Quanfu arrived late for the makeup, it was just in time for the dressing and makeup process. Throughout it all, only Mama Pei and Tong’er accompanied her, but Yü Qingci felt completely at ease.

In her past life, when she married, her mother had been overwhelmed with sorrow from beginning to end, weeping uncontrollably, and she herself had boarded the bridal sedan in tears.

In this life, the scene was even more pitiful in the eyes of outsiders, yet she felt nothing.

Before she could dwell on it, a spirit tablet wrapped in white silk was placed in her hands. A red veil was draped over her head, and she was helped into the bridal sedan.

The General’s mansion had sent an eight-man palanquin, a grand red sedan chair embroidered with gold patterns, carried by eight sturdy young men in matching red short robes. They looked energetic and imposing.

However, in front of this festive palanquin, two groups of men and women dressed in white mourning clothes, with hemp sashes and fillets, walked side by side, scattering white paper money as they went.

The stark contrast of the white and the red created an eerie atmosphere, silencing the crowds that lined the streets to watch.

Amid this strange mood, they finally arrived at the General’s mansion. After the sedan was set down, Yü Qingci was helped out. Only then did the crowd get a clear look at the bride.

She wore a bright red bridal gown embroidered with golden peony patterns, and her head was covered with a red veil embroidered with mandarin ducks playing in the water. Her figure was graceful, and her steps were steady. The most striking detail was the black spirit tablet she held in her hands, wrapped in a circle of white cloth.

The crowd fell completely silent.

She held the tablet as she bowed to heaven and earth, then was led through a series of turns before finally stopping and sitting down.

With the veil over her head, she listened to the sounds outside. Perhaps because there was no groom, the surroundings felt eerily quiet, with not even a single person trying to liven up the atmosphere. Occasionally, she could hear footsteps entering.

"Miss, you must be tired. Allow this old servant to remove your veil."

Yü Qingci stopped Mama Pei’s outstretched hand and removed the veil herself. The world before her eyes brightened.

This was her bridal chamber. The room was spacious and well-lit, with furniture and decorations that differed slightly from what she had imagined. Apart from the essential bed, cabinets, and a set of tables and chairs, the only touches of liveliness were the guifei couch by the window and the rosewood floor-length dressing case in the corner, which added a soft splash of color to the room.

Then she looked at the nanmu arhat bed she was sitting on. The bed curtains were made of indigo soft smoke-gauze with dark floral patterns, and the bed was covered with a set of plain-colored satin quilts embroidered with moon-white cloud patterns. The entire bridal chamber showed no sign of festivity.

This would be her home from now on.

Footsteps were heard outside again. This time, Mama Gui and Siqin pushed open the door and entered.

Seeing Siqin, Yü Qingci was not surprised. The last time Siqin had failed to carry out her mistress’s orders, she had disappeared from Ziteng Courtyard for several days. Unexpectedly, she had been sent by Madame Qiao as a accompanying maid.

As for Mama Gui, she was an elderly servant who had attended to Madame Qiao for many years. Though not as high-ranking as Mama Wu, she was still one of Madame Qiao’s confidantes. It seemed Madame Qiao had not given up and had planted her trusted servant here.

In addition to these two, there was another maid named Ling’er. These three were the personal servants who had entered the inner courtyard with her. There were also two other rooms of servants, along with the people her mother had sent. They were all placed in the outer courtyard to serve. If they performed well, they could later help her manage the outer estates, shops, and other properties.

Siqin entered and set down the tray in her hands, placing the snacks on the table. "Third Miss, you must be tired and hungry after such a long day. This servant has prepared two kinds of snacks. Please have a little to tide you over—dinner won’t be delivered from the kitchen until after the you hour."

Mama Pei was about to help Yü Qingci to the snacks, but Yü Qingci said, "There’s no rush. Since it seems no one will come to disturb us, let’s remove the makeup first, then eat."

Mama Pei then ordered Mama Gui and Siqin to fetch hot water. Siqin complied without a word, but Mama Gui stood still, staring directly at Yü Qingci.

When she saw that Yü Qingci paid no attention to her and simply followed Mama Pei’s instructions, Mama Gui reluctantly and slowly left.
